user_approved_operational_amendment.request: make the system RAM safety limit 1 GiB, continue waiting rather than self-stopping for low system availability, and fix the selector RAM problem

root_cause.ram_stall: The fold worker retained the full wide training frame, the full wide validation frame, the independent float32 selector matrix, and the selector's own allocations simultaneously. Lasso reached 21.9 GiB owned-process RSS. Suspending that process tree below the former 8 GiB system-available floor retained its allocations, so the former 10 GiB recovery threshold could not be reached without unrelated external memory release.
root_cause.terminal_warning: The supervised CLI emitted a terminal event through the generic emitter rather than ResearchLogSession.finish. The human STOP line was truthful, but the session-local terminal flag stayed false and produced a spurious missing-terminal-event warning after the clean manual stop.

selector_memory_lifecycle: encode the authenticated fold training predictors once into the existing C-contiguous float32 selector matrix
copy the fold training target into an independent int64 series
release and collect the original wide training and validation frames before the first opaque selector fit
release selector inputs after all selector fits
reload the exact fold frames once for evaluations and reject any predictor-order or scope-authentication mismatch
resume_semantics: the authenticated modeling matrix remains immutable and is not rebuilt
the eight sealed selector fits are reused
the incomplete fit_009 directory is archived and only fit_009 restarts
fold data loading and selector encoding repeat because they are transient memory inputs rather than sealed checkpoints
no evaluation or OOT result is reused or inspected because none exists
changes.terminal_finalization: complete, controlled-stop, and failed outcomes now use ResearchLogSession.finish so a clean Ctrl+C stop cannot be followed by the false missing-terminal-event warning

verified_behaviors: effective one-GiB system-available wait threshold with two-GiB hysteretic recovery
wide train and validation frames are unreachable before an opaque selector fit begins
selector matrix remains float32 and target remains int64
24 GiB owned-process hard cap remains unchanged
terminal outcomes finalize through the owning logging session

laptop_feasibility_assessment.expected_effect: releasing both wide source frames removes the avoidable simultaneous allocation during selector fitting
laptop_feasibility_assessment.conclusion: the implementation now has substantially more selector headroom, but the resumed bounded pilot must still prove fit_009 and every later heavy selector/model under the unchanged 24 GiB owned-process cap
